scenes.say: Empires come and go.
Iran has outlasted almost all of them.
So why does it still unsettle the world's great powers?
scenes.text: Why does it still | unsettle the world?

scenes.say: To understand, start at the very beginning.
scenes.title: From Persia to Iran

scenes.say: Middle Persian tradition speaks of as many as 240 kingdoms on the Iranian plateau.
scenes.label: Kingdoms on the Iranian plateau, in Middle Persian tradition
scenes.speak: Middle Persian tradition speaks of as many as two hundred and forty kingdoms on the Iranian plateau.

scenes.say: Bound not by one ruler, but by language, ritual and a shared cosmos.
Power moved across this world: from Balkh in the east, to Media, to Parthia, and finally to Pars.
scenes.title: Across the plateau

scenes.say: Pars gave Persia its name. But Persia was never the whole of Iran.
scenes.text: Persia was never | the whole of Iran

scenes.say: When one kingdom rose, it didn't abolish the others. It ruled over them.
scenes.title: Rule over, not erase

scenes.say: That gave the world the Shahanshah: the King of Kings.
An idea echoed in India: Rajadhiraja, and Chakravarti.
In the Iranian imagination, empire was not the annihilation of difference, but the orchestration of plurality.
scenes.kicker: Navroop Singh and Himja Parekh · Niti Shastra
scenes.text: "Empire was not annihilation of difference but orchestration of plurality."

scenes.say: In the 6th century BCE, Cyrus built the largest empire the world had yet seen.
scenes.speak: In the sixth century B C E, Cyrus built the largest empire the world had yet seen.

scenes.say: Alexander conquered it. Then he adopted its ways.
scenes.text: Alexander conquered it, | then adopted its ways

scenes.say: Persia's heirs became Rome's only true equals.
Then came the deepest rupture.
In the 7th century, the Sasanian empire fell to Arab armies.
scenes.speak: In the seventh century, the Sasanian empire fell to Arab armies.

scenes.say: Language, faith and rulers all changed.
One historian called what followed two centuries of silence.
Arabic has no P sound. So Pars became Fars, and Persian became Farsi.
scenes.title: Pars to Fars

scenes.say: But the Zoroastrians who fled to India kept the older word.
scenes.text: Those who fled to India | kept the old word

scenes.say: They are still called Parsis.
And Iran didn't die. It reshaped Islam itself.
Persians ran the Abbasid Caliphate. Turkic and Mongol conquerors became Persian kings.
scenes.title: Again and again

scenes.say: Again and again, the conqueror was absorbed.
The Safavids completed the restoration.
Twelver Shi'ism became the state faith: a firewall against Sunni rivals.
scenes.title: Faith fused with sovereignty

scenes.say: Faith fused with the state: the blueprint of modern Iran.
In the 1800s, Britain and Russia hollowed Iran out. In 1935, Persia became Iran.
scenes.title: A century of pressure
scenes.speak: In the eighteen-hundreds, Britain and Russia hollowed Iran out. In nineteen thirty-five, Persia became Iran.

scenes.say: In 1953, an Anglo-American coup toppled Mossadegh. Then came 1979, and revolution.
scenes.speak: In nineteen fifty-three, an Anglo-American coup toppled Mossadegh. Then came nineteen seventy-nine, and revolution.

scenes.say: The revolution hardened into a coercive state, increasingly run by the Revolutionary Guards.
Abroad, Iran built allies from Iraq to Lebanon to Yemen, to keep its wars far from home.
scenes.title: Allies across the region

scenes.say: For India, this is not a distant story.
scenes.title: Old cousins
items: The Parsis carry pre-Islamic Iran in India

scenes.say: Now, with the Gulf a tinderbox, Iran faces overwhelming pressure again.
History offers two paths: a long silence, or a profound renewal.
Because Iran measures history in centuries, not regimes.
